Slawno Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Sławno, Poland

Not demolished. Sławno's Jewish community numbered up to 250 people in 1871, though it lacked the funds to build its own funeral home despite expanding the cemetery's grounds in 1904. The necropolis was devastated during Kristallnacht in November 1938; by the 1960s, its matzevot had been stripped for use in road construction. By 1942, all of Sławno's Jews had been expelled, most to death camps in the east; a 1999 memorial plaque by sculptor Zygmunt Wujek commemorates the community, which had lived in the area since 1812.
